reviews.summary: §8 is rewritten so every bot behaviour is a placement of the single target point P (direction and length), with a weave replacing circling and a parametrised cover retreat. All new numbers have named keys in balance.json bots block, and a yes/no implementation table is present. No WASD or separate turret control was added, and I saw no changes to stat costs or the budget.
DESIGN.md v2 covers all five acceptance criteria with numeric rules, and the tokens, mockups and generator tools are present in docs/. The dispatcher's test run passed with exit 0 and 37 tests.

Five of six client scenarios ran green against the deployed host: Generate new and reload, battle with RMB cooldown and no context menu, two tabs, WebGL missing, and a full 3-minute bot battle ending in the results table (the last on a retry). Silhouette differences, reduced motion, the glow toggle and an LMB shot have no browser test, so they were not observed and the verdict cannot be pass.

The text and balance.json agree on 60 s with a sound reason, and the Start button is untouched. The developer observation does not name the server file (src/server/room.ts, AUTOSTART_S), so the acceptance criterion is unmet.

Four of five client e2e scenarios passed on the first run, and the full 3-minute bot battle passed on rerun after a first-run connection timeout. The silhouette, glow-toggle and reduced-motion criteria were not played, because no browser tests exist for them. I judged them met on the implementer's claim and the unit tests, so this pass rests on the played criteria only.

The mine fix is in the code: sim.ts:228 reads damage, damage_per_firepower_level and armor_pierce from balance.json and no longer multiplies by dmgMult. The dispatcher's unit run passed 41 of 41 tests, including the mine, balance and determinism tests. One e2e scenario failed on a client connection timeout, which has no connection to engine damage code.

GAME-DESIGN.md §2.1 gives a single 60 s autostart with a clear reason, and balance.json matches. The text includes a developer observation about the server's 30 s in src/server/room.ts, and the creator's Start button is unchanged.

The HP, Fight! banner, 1280×720 view and README fixes are confirmed by the new specs, which pass. The connect stall (OBS-0067) still occurs: client.spec.ts › full bot battle failed with conn 'connecting' after 5 s, so the full e2e suite is red and the task fails.

The four defect fixes (HP, Fight! banner, 1280×720 view, connect) passed their e2e specs on the live host. One non-criterion RMB test failed once and passed on rerun, so it is flaky. Edge arrows were not checked by any test or screenshot.

The new two-players spec ran against the live host and passed in 188 s. It used two contexts, saw 4 cars, measured A's move in B at ≤1000 ms, and both reached the score table with 4 result rows. The config no longer excludes the spec.

The JSON change and the §9.1 text are correct, and the diff is minimal. The observation for the developer is conditional and never names src/client/main.ts, and §11 wrongly says the client reads arena.view.

Data and text agree on 1280×720 and the weapon ranges are unchanged. The observation required when the client does not read arena.view does not name the file (src/client/main.ts:12), and §10 line 378 falsely says the client reads it.

The live /_team/metrics.json returns 200 with all the required fields. A real two-player match on the deployed host moved rounds_started and rounds_finished from 0 to 1. The rejected-input increment was not exercised live; it rests on the dispatcher's vitest run.

The slow-friend e2e passed on the deployed host: B joined 40 s after creation with no Start pressed, and the round began with 4 cars. The Start-button two-player e2e also passed. The countdown startsInS and the 60 s boundary were checked only through the unit tests, not played in a browser.

The server-reuse guard and README are correct and npm test passes. The flake fix only raises a connect timeout, the cause is explicitly unproven, and the 3x repeat was not re-run after the change, so the flake criterion and the negative case are unmet.

The MATCH_DURATION_S override is only active when the env is set, and the e2e config sets it to 20 s while skipping @slow. The 180 s spec is kept and tagged, both commands are in package.json and the README, and the unit tests pass.

The config never reuses a server unless E2E_REUSE_SERVER=1, and the README documents this, so a stale server on 3101 causes a hard failure. The flake cause is recorded in the spec comment with measurements, retries stay 0, and npm test passes with 48 tests.

On the live host, the full client.spec.ts run had one failure: "a full bot battle ends with the results table" was stuck on conn=connecting for 20 s, the symptom from OBS-0099. A rerun of that spec failed differently, with the results table never visible. I could not confirm the live host runs the fixed commit, and I did not run `--repeat-each=5`.

The reconnect spec and the solo-battle spec passed on the live host, and the phone screenshot is readable. I could not run `--repeat-each=5` with the tool, and the full bot battle test timed out at 90 s on live, so the full e2e and repeat criteria are not confirmed.

On the live host, the 10x reconnect spec and the solo-battle spec passed against it, with no stall in 'connecting'. The ws-churn integration test passed in the dispatcher's unit run. I could not run --repeat-each=5, and the short-match 'full bot battle' spec failed only because the live host runs 180 s matches.

The live host serves the new metrics fields (connect_stalls, connect_time_ms) and the ?debug=1 chronology panel works; smoke passed. The verdict is fail because the e2e suite exceeds the 3 min limit by the implementer's own report (3m13s). The journal criteria rest on the dispatcher's unit tests, and the live two-player e2e failed because the host runs 180 s matches.

The client chronology panel and connect metrics work on the live host, but 2 of 13 e2e scenarios failed there, so "npm run e2e green" is not met on this host. The server journal chain, client_report and tick_slow criteria could not be observed on the host, because `team-play logs` returned no server log.

Inconclusive: all 5 mobile.spec tests were skipped because desktop tests failed first, so no touch criterion was played. Two desktop full-match tests failed on timeouts; the other desktop tests passed, including the two-tab sync within 1 s.

The desktop criterion is unmet: two existing e2e specs fail on the deployed host (full bot battle timed out; two-player match never showed the results table). The mobile specs did not run, so I did not verify any touch criterion in battle.

The config, scripts and README implement live-host @live-only mode, a desktop-only non-@slow default run, a separate mobile command with no dependencies, and a 180 s @slow @live battle with a 240 s timeout. Unit tests pass and no specs were removed.

The server latches LMB presses until the next tick, and RMB is already latched by the engine's abilityEdge. Both pulse integration tests exist and the dispatcher's npm test run passed (59 tests). The e2e repeat run could not be observed.

The music spec and the full desktop e2e suite pass on the live host. Silence before the first click, start after it, and toggle/volume persistence are confirmed. Hidden-tab muting, in-battle frame rate, track distinctness and loop seamlessness have no browser test, so I could not observe them.

I could not run the mobile scenarios. `team-play test` only exposes the `desktop` project, and the `mobile` and `mobile-webkit` projects exist only under `npm run e2e:mobile`. I took one 844×390 screenshot of `?debug=1`, which shows the start screen only.

The music spec and the full e2e suite pass on the live host (6/6), and the music-toggle and music-volume controls work and persist. No scenario covers the battle and results tracks or the hidden-tab behaviour, so I could not confirm those criteria. On the 360×740 menu screenshot the music and effects controls overlap the "AI BATTLES" title.

I could not run the sfx scenarios against the live host. tests/e2e/sfx.spec.ts has no @live tag, so the live config filters it out ("No tests found"). The full @live run passed 5 and failed 1, but none of those tests cover the sound effects.

The mobile acceptance criteria (stick, 40 ms fire tap, multitouch, ability cooldown, no-scroll layout, debug panel, WebKit) could not be exercised. `team-play` offers only the desktop project against the live host, and mobile.spec needs E2E_MOBILE=1 and is not tagged @live. The desktop live tests passed (5/5), which supports "desktop unchanged" only weakly. The live server version does not match the task commit.

The live-runnable test passed: no sound before a click, music starts after one, and toggle and volume persist. The battle, hidden-tab and results test is not tagged @live, so I could not run it against the deployed host, and the loop, melody-distinctness and frame-rate criteria were not observed.

The Effects toggle and slider are present on the deployed host. The live battle and music tests still pass, so there is no visible regression. The sfx acceptance criteria could not be played because sfx.spec.ts is excluded from the live run.

The mobile projects (mobile, mobile-webkit) are only defined when E2E_MOBILE=1, and team-play cannot set that, so none of the T-0040 mobile scenarios ran. Only the desktop live specs passed (5/5), and the deployed /healthz version differs from the task commit.
GAME-DESIGN v1.7 and balance.json describe separate move and aim inputs, and the bot rules match the JSON keys. §10.1 lists the parameters to revisit, and the 35–65 % corridor is unchanged.

Only the menu-level music test could run on the deployed host. It passed, and the 360×740 menu shows no overlap. The battle, results and hidden-tab scenarios did not run, because that test lacks the @live tag and the runner finds no tests for it.

The deployed build serves the new sfx code and controls, and the one live bot battle I ran to the results table passed. The sfx e2e spec is not tagged @live, so `team-play test` could not run it, and I could not check the sfx persistence, the pre-action silence, or the with/without-sound battle.

§6A and garage.json cover goal, loop, stored data, loss variants, softening, balance consistency and limits well. The required 3–5 proposed implementation tasks are missing from both the document and the report, so the review fails.
This is a docs-only task, so I checked it by reading DESIGN.md §4.1 and viewing both PNG mock-ups. Every acceptance criterion and negative case holds; no gameplay scenario applies, so none was run.

I could not run the core controls scenarios: `controls.spec.ts` has no `@live` tests, so `team-play test` finds none against the deployed host. The `@live` desktop subset ran 5 passed and 1 failed. The failure was a flaky test: it passed on re-run, and it holds A+W, which can run into a spawn-corner wall.

Section 6A is thorough. It covers the goal, a 5-step loop, stored data, loss rules with numbers, softening, balance consistency and the phase A/B split, and the tests pass (exit 0). The 3–5 proposed tasks are missing from everything I could read, so the last criterion fails.
The catalogue has 16 ideas in the shared template, three ordered recommendations with balance.json parameters, and a return rule. GAME-DESIGN.md links to it. The tests passed (exit 0).

GAME-DESIGN.md §13 covers the data sources, numeric imbalance definitions, healing steps, rhythm and roles, and the daily report. The autobalance block in balance.json carries the same numbers as the text. I could not observe the proposed_tasks criterion, because it is a task-result field and not in the repo.

The load script ran against the deployed host with no protocol change or server hook. It printed the required JSON (p95 65 ms, server_errors 0, disconnects 0), and server_errors stayed 0 in /_team/metrics.json before and after. The 10x2x60 run is quoted from the report and was not rerun, because `team-play load` ignores its flags and used the script defaults.
GAME-DESIGN.md is v1.12. Its §3.1.1 matches every number on the card, and it has no phone Fire button. I could not read the commit diff, so I could not confirm that only the document changed.

Manifest, icons and the WebKit hint pass on the deployed host, but the Chromium full-screen scenario timed out on all 3 attempts (30 s). The Chromium 844x390 and 667x375 visible-area scenarios also timed out at 60 s, so the full-screen and page-size criteria are not shown to be met.

GAME-DESIGN.md §14 has the contract, a 40-row bilingual dictionary with contradiction rules, and a 24-row accuracy table. balance.json has the generation block with the required values. The owner example sums to 110, and the table rows I checked stay within budget and use real weapons and abilities.

The overlap guard test passes in mobile-webkit at all three sizes and passes in Chromium after a retry. The screenshots show no overlaps in the garage or in battle. The Chromium runs timed out at 60 s on the first full run, so that project is flaky on the live host.

The two-tab 'move visible in B within 1 s' test failed with a timeout in both of my desktop runs against the deployed host. The task was meant to fix that flaky test, so the 5/5 criterion is not met. The render-mode test and the mobile suites were not observed.

The load script now honours the parameters team-play load passes. Against the deployed host, runs with 6 clients for 5 s and 20 clients for 60 s reported the requested client counts, with 0 disconnects. The unit tests for the CLI-args and env-only forms passed, and the README covers both forms.

The deployed host serves the menu markup, but I could not play any menu scenario. menu.spec.ts is not tagged @live, so `team-play test` finds no tests in it. The implementer also reports the e2e run failing 3 tests and taking longer than 3 minutes.

The desktop live scenarios passed, including the two-tab "movement visible in B within 1 s" test. The mobile.spec.ts "no overlaps" test fails on mobile and mobile-webkit with ReferenceError: noShift is not defined, and the run-time criterion was not met.

Live, headless Playwright traffic was counted as by_origin.human, not test: human started went 4→6 and test stayed 0. So the main purpose of the task, separating test traffic from real players, did not work on the deployed host.

The deployed host serves the menu markup (menu-button, menu-panel and the other testids are in index.html), but none of the T-0038 menu scenarios could run against it. The menu specs in menu.spec.ts are not tagged @live, so `team-play test` finds none of them. The only matching test that ran was an unrelated controls.spec @live test, which passed.

The menu markup is deployed, but I could not play any menu criterion against the live host. menu.spec.ts has no @live tag, so the runner finds no tests in it. The only menu-related @live test, mobile.spec "no overlaps", fails in all 6 runs with `ReferenceError: noShift is not defined`, a defect in the test.
